rules.title: Santa Ana ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental property in Santa Ana. The ordinance targets tools that set rents using nonpublic competitor data such as real-time rents, lease renewals and occupancy levels. Tenants may sue directly for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties, and need only prove the landlord used prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees; injunctive relief and damages available to affected tenants

coverage.summary: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits; operates alongside state antitrust laws.
coverage.other_conditions: Limited to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.effective_date_note: The document reports approval for a first reading on Feb. 17, 2026, with a final vote set for March 3, 2026. It does not state the final adoption or effective date.

result.doc_summary: A February 2026 city press release, republished by PublicCEO, reports that the Santa Ana City Council approved a first reading on Feb. 17, 2026 of an ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rentals. A final vote was set for March 3. The ordinance exempts tools using only public or aggregate historical data and affordable-housing compliance tools. It allows tenant suits for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees. The document also briefly mentions Santa Ana's existing rent stabilization and eviction-protection ordinance without details.
